A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QWHA work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across Appendix D's expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSQA and GSM8k accuracy experiments, quantization-error analyses, ablations, and training-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds temperature sensitivity, initialization and inference measurements, and training-curve analyses.

M1.justification: Equation 7 changes the reported AdaAlloc allocation rule from channel norms of weight error ΔWQ to activation-weighted error ΔWQX. The adapter architecture, coefficient selection, and value refinement remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 still calls AdaAlloc(p, ΔWQ), leaving the implementation correspondence unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, GSM8k, the same seven commonsense benchmarks, and WikiText-2 calibration data. GSM8k training was already documented in v1's Appendix D.1; v4's clearer training/test description does not establish added coverage. The new resource measurements extend evaluation procedures.

E2.justification: Corresponding accuracy, ablation, and training comparisons retain the same comparators, including CLoQ, SHiRA, LoCA, SSH, and the hybrid adapter variants. The added resource comparisons reuse methods already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v4 adds initialization profiling and inference throughput/memory protocols, specifying 2048-token prefill, 64-token generation, and batch size 128. Table 8 also revises the reported QWHA scale from 4000 to 4000/din, explained as an existing implementation detail rather than demonstrated retuning. Other main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3 and D.8 add a focused temperature sweep and loss/gradient-norm diagnostics for 4-bit LLaMA-3.2-3B. D.6 adds initialization-memory decomposition. Existing adapter, parameter-budget, refinement, and group-size analyses remain; Figure 8 removes the pretrained-weight distribution comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables and training curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The main accuracy and training-efficiency values are retained, but v4 substantially expands resource and diagnostic results. New Tables 17–20 report initialization costs, inference throughput of 184.6 tokens/sec for WHA versus 188.1 for LoRA, and memory of 52.68 GB for QWHA versus 59.53 for CLoQ. Temperature results and training trajectories are added, and Figure 8's distributions are revised.

T1.justification: Equation 7 revises the mathematical definition of channel allocation. Appendix B.2 also changes the justification for applying random-matrix rank conditions, invoking approximately normal coefficients and nearly zero cross-row correlations. The formal rank-condition equations, Proposition 1 and its proof, and objective-reduction derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a single-transform WHT adapter, quantization-aware allocation and refinement, improved low-bit accuracy, and faster training than conventional FT-based adapters. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v4 explains why extreme temperatures harm allocation, interprets similar convergence despite different gradient norms, and attributes initialization/inference costs to SVD, scatter operations, and transform implementations. These add specific mechanism explanations and operating qualifications without substantially changing the main interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly explains nominal versus effective scaling and adds parameter counts by projection, layer, and model. v4 clarifies GSM8k evaluation and resource-measurement settings. A new reproducibility statement describes supplementary code, setup instructions, and preprocessing scripts; the existing GitHub link is retained, and availability beyond the PDFs is unverified.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the positioning relative to LoRA-based QA-PEFT and Fourier-related adapters is retained. The local wording refinement from sparse adapters to FT-based adapters does not materially change that positioning.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized explanatory and terminology edits, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, and reorganizes Appendix D, including combining training-time and training-memory discussions. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix gains parameter-count, temperature, initialization, and inference tables plus a two-panel training-curve figure. Figure 8 is redrawn with revised curves and axes and without pretrained-weight overlays. These substantially expand the displayed evidence, while most earlier figures and tables are retained with layout and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through clearer scaling documentation and adds useful checks of temperature choice, optimization behavior, and initialization/inference costs. The main accuracy evidence and proofs remain largely unchanged. Benefits are tempered by the unreconciled Equation 7/Algorithm 1 allocation description and a new numerical overstatement: Table 20 implies an 11.5% memory reduction relative to CLoQ, whereas the text claims 13.0%.
